## Natural history notes

A microscopic freshwater green alga belonging to the desmids, characterized by flattened, bilaterally symmetrical cells divided into two semicells by a deep central constriction. Micrasterias truncata has broadly rounded semicells with several deeply divided lobes, but its overall outline is more compact and less intricately branched than species such as Micrasterias rotata. It occurs primarily in acidic to slightly acidic freshwater habitats, including bog pools, ponds, peatlands, and shallow vegetated wetlands. Like many desmids, it is most common in relatively clean, low-nutrient waters and contributes to freshwater primary production while also serving as a useful indicator of aquatic habitat and water-chemistry conditions.
